title: Borrowing, Personal Ownership & Independence Standard
summary: Borrowing between therapists is not permitted as a normal workplace practice. Every therapist is expected to come prepared, respect ownership, and every colleague has the absolute right to say no.

sections.title: The Standard
paragraphs: At Zura Spa, borrowing between therapists and colleagues is not permitted as a normal workplace practice.
This applies to money, food, personal belongings, clothing, toiletries, work kits, massage tools, personal equipment, personal supplies, and other privately owned items.
Every therapist is expected to develop a high level of personal responsibility, independence, planning, discipline and ownership.
Come prepared for your work and personal needs. Do not make another colleague responsible for supplying what you should reasonably have provided for yourself.
At Zura Spa, every colleague also has the absolute right to say NO when asked to lend money, food, a personal item, a work kit, clothing, supplies, or any privately owned property.
A colleague does not need to explain or justify why they do not want to lend something. "No" is a complete and acceptable answer.
Refusing to lend must never result in anger, pressure, mockery, gossip, retaliation, exclusion, bullying, hostility, or emotional manipulation.

The purpose of this standard is not to make the team uncaring. It is to create a safe professional environment where people can work together without financial dependence, personal pressure, hidden obligations or conflict over belongings.

sections.title: 1. Why Zura Spa Has a No-Borrowing Standard
paragraphs: Borrowing may appear harmless: "It's just ₦2,000." "Let me use your kit." "Just give me some of your food." "I'll return it later."
But repeated borrowing can gradually create unhealthy workplace relationships.

It can lead to dependence, entitlement, pressure, resentment, arguments, unpaid debts, damaged belongings, unequal relationships, fear of saying no, bullying, favouritism, expectations of reciprocity, and distraction from work.
For this reason, Zura Spa chooses to remove the problem at its source. Instead of managing borrowing conflicts, we avoid creating borrowing relationships in the first place.

sections.title: 2. The Purpose of the Standard
paragraphs: The standard exists to encourage therapists to become independent, responsible, prepared, disciplined, thoughtful, and comfortable with ownership.
A therapist should be able to come to work without depending on another therapist to supply basic personal or professional needs.
Think ahead about what you need. Bring required items before reporting for duty. Manage money, supplies and personal needs responsibly.
Consider tomorrow's needs today rather than repeatedly depending on someone else when a need arises.
Therapists should become comfortable saying: "This belongs to me, and I am responsible for it." and equally: "That belongs to Thr. Jane, so I do not expect access to it."

sections.title: 3. The Mindset
paragraphs: The Zura therapist should have the mindset: "I am responsible for preparing myself for work and managing my personal needs."
The therapist should not routinely think "If I don't have it, I'll ask somebody." Instead: "If I will need it, I should plan for it."
This applies to transport money, feeding, toiletries, personal care items, work tools, clothing, personal supplies, and other predictable needs.
Independence does not mean that nobody can ever receive help. It means that dependence on colleagues should not become the system through which a therapist manages their life or work.

sections.title: 4. Everyone Has the Right to Say No
paragraphs: A major part of this standard is protecting the right of every colleague to control their own belongings.
If Thr. Jane asks Thr. Clara: "Please can I borrow ₦5,000?" Thr. Clara is completely free to say: "No, please." That should be the end of the discussion.

The person asking should not ask repeatedly, demand an explanation, become angry, make the colleague feel guilty, say "But I always help you," say "It's just small money," call the colleague stingy, tell other therapists about the refusal, stop speaking to the colleague, refuse to assist them professionally later, or try to get other therapists to pressure them.
Nobody at Zura Spa should be afraid to say NO.

sections.title: 5. Borrowing Out of Fear Is Not Consent
paragraphs: A person may technically say "Okay, take it" while actually feeling unable to refuse.

This can happen where the person asking is more senior, the borrower is more dominant, there is peer pressure, the colleague fears being disliked, excluded, or retaliated against, or the colleague has repeatedly been pressured before.
For this reason, Zura Spa does not want employees put in the position where they must repeatedly decide whether refusing a colleague will damage the relationship.
The standard removes that pressure: do not ask colleagues to lend you their personal resources.

sections.title: 6. No Borrowing of Money
paragraphs: Therapists should not routinely lend or borrow money from one another.

This includes cash, transfers, airtime purchased on credit, transport money, feeding money, personal bills, emergency loans between colleagues, "I'll pay you when salary comes," and repeated small loans.
The amount does not change the principle. A ₦500 loan can create the same emotional tension as a ₦50,000 loan if it becomes a source of conflict.

sections.title: 7. No Borrowing of Food
paragraphs: Food belongs to the person who purchased or brought it unless they freely choose to offer or share it.
There is a difference between voluntary sharing — "Thr. Jane, would you like some?" — and borrowing or pressuring — "Give me some of your food; I'll replace it tomorrow."
No therapist should feel obligated to share lunch, give away snacks, buy food for another therapist, split what they brought, or explain why they do not want to share.
A voluntary gift is different from borrowing.

sections.title: 8. No Borrowing of Personal Belongings
paragraphs: Therapists should not assume access to another person's clothes, shoes, makeup, hair products, toiletries, chargers, phones, earphones, bags, or personal items.
Always respect ownership. If it is not yours, do not use it merely because it is available.

sections.title: 9. No Borrowing of Personal Work Kits
paragraphs: Every therapist is expected to be responsible for the work tools or personal kit they are required to maintain.
Do not repeatedly rely on another therapist's work kit, massage tools, personal supplies, grooming materials, uniform items, or other assigned personal equipment.
A therapist should not become unable to perform their responsibility simply because another colleague refuses to lend them something. That indicates a preparation problem that should be corrected.

sections.title: 10. Company Property Is Different From Personal Property
paragraphs: Shared Zura Spa resources are not treated as one therapist's personal property.
Where the company provides equipment, supplies, towels, tools, consumables, or shared facilities, they should be used according to the appropriate operational standard.
The No-Borrowing Standard primarily addresses personal resources and individually assigned property.
Company equipment should still be properly requested where necessary, used responsibly, returned correctly, and reported when unavailable or damaged.

sections.title: 11. When a Genuine Need Arises
paragraphs: If a therapist genuinely lacks something necessary for work, the first response should not be "Who can lend me?"
The correct response should be: IDENTIFY → COMMUNICATE → ESCALATE → SOLVE.
Example: "SM, I do not have the required item for today's session. Please advise on what I should do."
This gives leadership visibility and allows a proper solution to be found. A work-related need should not silently become another therapist's personal responsibility.

sections.title: 12. If Borrowing Must Occur
paragraphs: The default remains: NO BORROWING.
However, where there is an exceptional situation in which borrowing genuinely needs to occur, it must not be treated as a private arrangement between two colleagues.
The following leadership roles should be informed and engaged as appropriate: Manager, Staff Manager (SM), and Supervisor (SP).
The leader acts as a mediator and witness to the arrangement.

The purpose is to ensure that nobody is being pressured, both parties understand the arrangement, the item or amount is clear, expectations are clear, there is no later confusion, and the relationship does not become a source of conflict.
If the matter does not justify involving a leader, that is often a good indication that the borrowing should simply not happen.

sections.title: 13. Procedure for an Exceptional Borrowing Request
paragraphs: Where borrowing is genuinely unavoidable, follow this procedure.

sections.title: Step 1 — Do Not Pressure the Person
paragraphs: Ask once, if permitted by leadership. The colleague remains free to say "No."

sections.title: Step 2 — Inform the Appropriate Leader
paragraphs: The Manager, SM or SP should know what is being requested, who is involved, and why the exception is necessary.

sections.title: Step 3 — Confirm That the Lender Is Willing
paragraphs: The leader should ensure that the person is not lending because of fear, pressure, seniority, friendship obligations, or emotional manipulation.

sections.title: Step 4 — Make the Arrangement Clear
paragraphs: Where money or valuable property is involved, clarify what was given, the amount where applicable, and the expected return or repayment arrangement, if any.

sections.title: Step 5 — Keep the Matter Private and Professional
paragraphs: The borrowing arrangement should not become a topic for the wider team.

sections.title: 14. Zura Spa Will Not Enforce Unauthorized Personal Loans
paragraphs: If two therapists ignore this standard and privately lend or borrow money, food, property, work kits, or personal belongings, Zura Spa will not become a debt-collection service for that private unauthorized arrangement.
A therapist who chooses to lend contrary to the standard does so at their own risk.
They should not later expect management to force repayment, management to deduct another therapist's salary, colleagues to pressure the borrower, or workplace conflict to be created over recovery.
This consequence exists deliberately to discourage staff from creating private lending relationships at work. If you do not want to risk losing it, do not lend it.
This does not mean that dishonesty, theft, fraud or deliberate misconduct is acceptable. Those are separate conduct matters and may be investigated or disciplined independently.
Zura Spa does not guarantee or enforce unauthorized personal borrowing arrangements between colleagues.

sections.title: 15. Why This Protects the Lender Too
paragraphs: Without this rule, a therapist may repeatedly lend because "I didn't want her to feel bad." Then later become angry when repayment is delayed.
The better protection is: Do not enter the arrangement in the first place.
The standard gives every therapist organizational permission to say: "We are not permitted to borrow from one another." This removes much of the personal awkwardness.

sections.title: 16. Borrowing Should Not Create Power Between Colleagues
paragraphs: Financial and personal dependence can create unhealthy power relationships.
Someone may later feel: "I helped you, so you should help me." "You owe me." "Remember when I gave you money?" "You can't refuse me after everything I've done for you."
This is exactly the type of hidden obligation the standard is designed to prevent.
Work responsibilities should be performed because they are professional responsibilities — not because one colleague owes another a personal favour.

sections.title: 17. Borrowing Must Never Become Bullying
paragraphs: The following are unacceptable: repeatedly asking after being refused, making fun of someone for refusing, calling someone stingy, pressuring someone because they earn more, telling people they are selfish, using leadership position to obtain personal items, threatening the working relationship, withdrawing professional cooperation because someone refused, getting friends to pressure the person, and making someone feel guilty for protecting their belongings.
This is no longer simply borrowing. It becomes a professional conduct and safe-workplace issue.

sections.title: 18. Refusal Must Not Affect Teamwork
paragraphs: Thr. Jane may refuse to lend Thr. Clara money today. Tomorrow, if they are assigned together for a 4-hands massage, they are still expected to communicate, synchronize, support each other, perform their duties, and treat each other professionally.
Personal refusal must never become: "Since you refused me, I won't help you." Professional responsibilities remain professional responsibilities.

sections.title: 19. What the Opposite Looks Like
paragraphs: The opposite of this standard is a team where borrowing becomes normal.
It may begin with "Can I use your charger?" then "Buy food for me." then "Borrow me ₦5,000." then "I'll pay you next week."
Eventually the workplace develops debtors, creditors, arguments, favouritism, pressure, hidden resentment, personal alliances, fear of refusing, gossip about money, and conflict over property.
The team begins managing personal financial relationships instead of focusing on clients and professional responsibilities. That is not the workplace culture Zura Spa wants.

sections.title: 20. Why Zura Spa Will Not Tolerate a Borrowing Culture
paragraphs: A borrowing culture creates risks that have little to do with massage but can seriously damage the team.

Zura Spa will therefore not normalize repeated borrowing, persistent requests for money, pressure to share belongings, borrowing work tools instead of preparing, dependence on colleagues for daily needs, conflicts over repayment, retaliation after refusal, debt collection inside the workplace, emotional manipulation connected to lending, or use of leadership position to obtain personal assistance.
The aim is not punishment. The aim is to create an environment where everyone can come to work without being financially or personally responsible for another adult colleague.

sections.title: 21. Impact of Borrowing on the Team
paragraphs: Borrowing can damage relationships, create unequal relationships, create fear, produce bullying, distract leadership, affect massage teamwork, and weaken personal responsibility.
Two therapists may begin as friends and eventually stop speaking because of ₦5,000 that was not repaid. The personal conflict then enters the workplace.
One therapist may gradually become another therapist's lender, food provider, emergency fund, or source of supplies. This creates dependence instead of equality.
A therapist may become afraid that saying no will cause rejection, gossip, hostility, loss of friendship, or poor cooperation.
People who are naturally generous, quiet or conflict-avoidant can become targets for repeated requests.
Management may eventually have to spend time dealing with "She owes me," "She took my item," "She refused to give me money," or "She promised to pay." These are avoidable workplace conflicts.

A personal debt between two therapists may lead to tension during 4-hands massage, room preparation, handovers, cleaning, assessments, and team communication. The client may eventually feel the consequences.
If a therapist always knows "Someone will give me," there is less pressure to plan, budget, prepare, replace missing items, and take responsibility.

sections.title: 22. The Culture We Want to Create
paragraphs: We want therapists who are independent — "I can manage my responsibilities."
Prepared — "I think ahead."
Disciplined — "I manage what I have."
Responsible — "I own my choices."
Comfortable with boundaries — "I can respectfully say no."
Respectful of ownership — "If something belongs to Thr. Jane, I do not feel entitled to it."
Comfortable owning — "I should gradually acquire and maintain the things I personally need."
The goal is to create adults who can work together closely while remaining personally responsible for themselves.

sections.title: 23. What Therapists Should Do
list: Come prepared for meals where applicable.
Keep emergency transport arrangements where reasonably possible.
Ask leadership for guidance when a work-related resource is unavailable.
Say no respectfully when they do not want to lend.
Keep personal financial matters away from work relationships.

sections.title: 24. What Therapists Should Not Do
list: Routinely lend money to colleagues at work.
Use another person's work kit because they failed to prepare.
Take something because they intend to return it later.
Assume friendship gives access to another person's property.
Repeatedly ask after being told no.
Use leadership position to pressure someone.
Use emotional stories to manipulate colleagues into lending.
Turn colleagues into regular sources of financial support.
Bring personal debt disputes into client service.
Ask management to enforce an unauthorized personal loan.
Create sides within the team over borrowing disputes.

sections.title: 25. Correction and Accountability
paragraphs: At Zura Spa: Forgetting an item once + correcting the preparation problem = learning. Encountering a genuine need + escalating appropriately = responsibility. Being asked to lend + respectfully saying no = acceptable professional boundary. Receiving a no + accepting it immediately = maturity.

But: Repeated borrowing = performance/culture concern. Pressuring colleagues to lend = conduct concern. Retaliating because someone refused = serious conduct concern. Bullying someone into sharing money, food or belongings = serious disciplinary concern. Taking another person's property without permission = not borrowing; it is a separate serious conduct matter.

sections.title: 26. The Zura Spa No-Borrowing Standard
paragraphs: PLAN → PREPARE → PROVIDE FOR YOURSELF → RESPECT OWNERSHIP → ASK LEADERSHIP WHEN NECESSARY

Every therapist should ask: What will I need today? Have I prepared for it? Is this my responsibility to provide for myself? Am I making another therapist responsible for something I should manage? If they say no, can I accept it respectfully? If this is genuinely necessary for work, have I informed the appropriate leader?
YOU HAVE THE RIGHT TO OWN.
YOU HAVE THE RIGHT TO SAY NO.
YOU DO NOT HAVE THE RIGHT TO PRESSURE ANOTHER PERSON TO SHARE.
YOU ARE EXPECTED TO PLAN FOR YOUR OWN NEEDS.
UNAUTHORIZED PERSONAL LOANS ARE NOT GUARANTEED OR ENFORCED BY ZURA SPA.
IF AN EXCEPTIONAL BORROWING ARRANGEMENT IS NECESSARY, MANAGER, SM OR SP MUST BE INVOLVED.
The standard is not "Do not help people." The standard is "Do not build workplace relationships around dependence, debt and obligation."
We want a team that can support one another professionally without becoming financially or personally dependent on one another.
BE RESPONSIBLE. BE PREPARED. RESPECT OWNERSHIP. RESPECT NO. PROTECT THE SAFE SPACE.

remember: Come prepared. Respect ownership. "No" is a complete and acceptable answer.
